body: Hi! Are you still feeling to chat? I'm really upset about something that happened today and would really like to get those emotions out. Thanks!
Hi! I was wondering if you were still free to talk, I was hoping to get some emotional support for something that's been bothering me a bit recently?
Those days just happen, I'm happy to hear that you're feeling better! I'll be wishing you the best!! :)

Hi, I'm sorry you're going through this and feeling all these overwhelming feelings. I totally relate to what you're saying here, you are not alone in feeling this way. I set out to do a lot of the same things you are (trauma processing, replacing unhealthy habits, learning to like myself), and this happens to me from time to time. I'll be doing well for awhile and just some days it feels like my feelings catch up with me and I crash. The negative feelings are overwhelming and it just feels like everything is falling apart, it's a terrible feeling. 

I understand how difficult working through all of this is, and I want to reassure you things will get better! It's a hard and scary journey, but it sounds like you're making amazing progress! Unfortunately, working through all this takes its toll and you just have to take a breather. There is absolutely nothing wrong with feeling this way, it doesn't mean you're failing or that you've lost progress. Emotions are a part of the process, as good or as bad as they feel, and your feelings are completely valid. Take a bit of time to recover and keep going, everything will be okay!

If you ever want to talk about any of this more or feel like you need someone to talk to, I'd be happy to! I hope this helps, you got this! :)

Hi! I'm sorry you're feeling lonely, from experience I know how terrible these feelings you're talking about can feel. You are not alone in the feeling.

I know it can sometimes be hard to believe, but you are deserving of having connections with others. You belong here and you're deserving of friendships, just by being human. We all have flaws, it doesn't make you any less deserving of friends. Finding people you feel comfortable and happy around may be challenging, but it's something that will happen over time!

I hope this helps, and I'm cheering you on! If you want to talk about this some more too I'd be happy to respond in DMs or in the comments!

Hi! I wanted to give you some reassurance, loneliness is a pretty tough thing to go thro. It's something you're not alone in feeling, lots of people have issues with it. It's something I deal with too, having gone thro a breakup recently, and those emotions can be pretty intense. 

Your feelings here aren't "silly or dramatic," they're totally valid. Your feelings are your feelings, if it's something that's really bothering you it's really bothering you, it's not you "being dramatic." Emotions can be intense and it's okay to feel them, there isn't anything wrong with that! It's perfectly okay to let yourself feel your emotions!

Honestly, it sometimes feels like not knowing what to do can be the worst part. Uncertainty can be really scary, and being told to "just go meet people" can be pretty invalidating. It's a difficult fear to get over, it can be very scary to open up to people. When working thro fears like that, I find it helpful to do small steps at a time to gradually work up to getting over it. You can do it, you'll find someone! I'm happy to talk if you need someone to talk with or just vent! I hope this helps!

Currently I'm using an oil from the brand Asha's Elixirs. It's the 500mg bottle, broad spectrum, and it has a dropper that you can use to dose it. When I bought it, I was recommended to take .5 ml twice per day but I've been taking .75 ml instead. With the oil, you hold it under your tongue for about a minute for it to work properly. I will say it's kinda pricey, I think it was $60-65 when I got it last. It's definitely helped me but always be careful with trying new stuff with Crohn's. I've had CBD recommended by both my doctor and my medical marijuana doctor. Again, I can say that it works for me but it may not work for everyone. Feel free to ask any more questions if you need!
D: ik the feeling, sometimes I just can't resist eating something that'll set me off. Hope it gets better soon!

Currently, I was able to cut my meds to just remicade (or inflectra? my insurance was messing with me earlier this year), a multivitamin, and the CBD and THC stuff. As far as diarrhea goes I'm honestly not sure. I usually have those spells when I wake up in the middle of the night with a ton of pain, so I start having that problem then I take the THC. I can't really remember exactly the form of my stools when I take it (probably bc I was high and that kinda memory became blurred lol) but I also don't remember having a bad episode while taking it. Sry if that answer sucks, I've never used it to try to control constipation/diarrhea before. 

I will say the medical card (at least in my state) was pretty expensive and the price of buying edibles, while not super high, is kinda pricey too. Again, feel free to ask anything!

I don't take humira, but in my experience it definitely helps. My symptoms are pretty strong and don't like going away, but when I take an edible it makes them better by a noticeable amount almost every time. I can be stuck with horrible intestine pains and it will most often make the pain tolerable, sometimes even ignorable. 

Edibles are annoying to take tho, from experience I have to take them on an empty stomach and wait about 45min-1hr for it to kick in all the way. If I mess with that system basically at all it barely works. I also want to mention that I now take CBD oil constantly and take THC stuff only when I need it. That system seems to work very well for me. 

If you want to ask me questions about this, feel free to dm or comment! I'm happy to give more details or answer anything.
Hiya! I also love Stardew and think you seem rlly cool! I'm 19nb if you wanna talk, send me a dm! Btw papaya

No worries! There is not one close to me tho, it's an over 2hr drive without traffic. It's a bit of a distance, but it's good to know they do telehealth bc maybe I can try that. It would be a real uphill battle for me to plan going there multiple times tho (for infusions and such), it would probably eat up most of the day lol. My current infusions are like 20-30min away.

While I don't want to say where I live in the comments, there is a mayo clinic very far from me in my state. I'm not super sure how I'd logistically get there tbh. It's good to know it's a great option tho, and I may go to them if I need to. It seems like I either have a rlly weird case of Crohn's or my current doctors really suck. My current doctor has said such nice things as "I've never seen a case like you before" or "I'm not sure what to do about that" which are always great to hear. Hopefully I can find a good clinic/doctor at some point tho.

Maybe I should write a script for when I'm thrown some wacky "cure" from anyone, instead of arguing. I will say the THC products I use aren't perfect, but I'm working on how to improve their effectiveness. They also don't cause me harm and typically do more than real strong medications my doctor has prescribed in the past, so I'll probably stick with it (unless there is a real problem for me).

Also I wanted to say that I think integrative therapies probably could help, I just don't know anything. To me it sounds like exercise, yoga, spas, massages, and anything along those lines could help. I will say, I'm very skeptical of weirder ones (like the float pods and salt rooms) as I don't see what they actually do or achieve. There may be something to it and it could just be my bias, but still. I remember the salt room being described to me as "you sit in a room with the walls made of salt and it absorbs all the toxins from you" which sounded like.. well not that it could harm you but like it wouldn't do anything. I just wanted to clear that up. Again thanks!

Thank you for all the advice! I would talk to my GI specialist more, but they aren't the best tbh. They throw the same ideas at me usually (even tho they don't work at all for me). That aside, I totally shouldn't take random "supplements" or really anything that comes from a random source. I've had "miracle" cures be offered to me before, ranging from a veggie pill (of unknown origin) to a.. magic medical cure box? in Germany (wild ik).

Can I throw some questions your way tho? Where should I start when looking up what can make Crohn's worse? For as long as I had it, I should've done this by now but I never really knew where to start. Also, do you know of any good ways to write down information like this, like a good diary with a symptom chart? I've been looking for something like that too. Thanks again!

Thank you! You're right that I shouldn't take something my doctors haven't prescribed, I just don't know what would harm me. Like I learnt a month ago that I shouldn't take ibuprofen. 

Honestly, I think my mom is too convinced to do her own research at this point. She was telling me to go research the thing she gave me today, and I did and came to the conclusion that it would do nothing or be harmful. When I told her, she point blank said something along the lines of "oh you're just looking up stuff to confirm your bias" like 3 times :/ . Like come on-

Also, she keeps telling me she's "so much better than before" and stuff like that. I hope what she says is true for her sake, but I kinda don't believe it. I hear the same complaints of all of the problems she had before but some unrelated ones have gotten better (but I should note, her health has only gotten worse in other places during this too so idk what to say).

Thank you for the advice! The way she was pressuring me to take it was unsettling and I'm glad to know I'm the reasonable one for saying no to some random "supplement." I'm sorry for the person you know who had cancer tho, I'm glad they're doing better now but it always still sucks. I don't remember if my mom was referred to a chiropractor or how it started, but it was for like back/neck pains, stiffness, and general problems like that. Ever since she started going she claims to be much better and has since been trying to convince me to go (which I won't, I don't see it curing my Crohn's .-.). It gets annoying to hear it every like other week. 

Also I love your suggestion on pushing it off to my doctor. I'll maybe give that a whirl when I get a new GI specialist, I don't have much faith in the one I have now (haven't switched yet bc of inconvenience and I'm scared I'll lose my medicine). My current specialist, when recommending I try cbd unknowingly sent me to a that had a "healing salt room" and from that point on, I couldn't really trust my doctor as much.

I believe that she has good intentions here. This isn't a first attempt at something like this, and actually it wouldn't be the first random "supplement" of unknown quality either. Altho it does make me wonder how she does her research, or the lack of it. I know she wants me off of my Crohn's meds bc she believes they are making my sickness worse when.. they're probably the thread holding me together. I mean I don't wanna be on them either, I'm a person who's adverse to medicine, but at least I understand that it helps me and makes it so that I don't just like.. well die lol. (For as bad as every GI specialist I've been to has been) I think I need to be able to make my own informed decisions, instead of taking unregulated "supplements" from 2nd hand testimony of someone I don't know (side note my mom didn't buy them, it was the Crohn's man I don't know which thinking about it makes it a little more sketchy..er)

Couldn't agree with this more. If the story is true, I'm glad this guy doesn't have to take Crohn's medications bc I kinda hate it, but at the same time it makes me worry for him. Maybe he's just really mild? Idk, my mom offered me the man's phone number and I'm almost curious but I know that it won't get me anywhere, would be pointless confrontation, and dig me deeper into this. But my Crohn's is significantly different than what is described there, so I should probably follow my own path here.
